question.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=4 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & ⇒ & v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 4x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =4x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 4\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}4x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =4x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2}-4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2}+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =4(\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(0))+4(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =4(\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 1-0\cdot 0)+4(0-1) \\  & =2\pi -4.\end{aligned}
$$
